differences.what: Gable: the twin windows' heads are pointed, two lights 0.63 m wide with their points at 5.87 m, not the kit's flat-headed pair (T-2423)

Bay: a small dark stop at each spring of every light's casing, on its outer edge (T-2457)

Entrance: the posts broad plain piers, 0.22 m across (T-2425)

Entrance: steps up to the floor between two cheek walls in the posts' line, their tops sloping with the steps, where the kit's porch had its lattice to grade (T-2425)

Built as a 0.12 m bar and one light under a low gable, 0.17 m at the jambs and 0.39 m at the middle: rendered, its south slope lies within 1 px of the print's (631, 627 and 623 px at 700, 710 and 720 px), its foot and apex 4 px high, and the apex at the door's middle, 10 px north of the print's; the glass's dark north part (what it reflects) is not modelled

Tower: each light's casing is carried round its pointed head as an arched band, the smooth face round it, with no head board or drip cap, where the model's lights stood in square-headed casings (T-2521)

Re-read through T-2523's camera (T-2456 took them at 158.7 px a metre, where it draws 112.6): shafts 0.49 m at s -0.47 and 1.365 m, the gateway 1.255 m clear, caps 0.56 m from 1.61 to 1.98 m, finials to 2.385 m, the base 0.32 m and the bars 0.349 m apart to 0.83 m, the first bar against the north plinth at 345 px as the print draws it; rendered, the shafts within 2 px, the caps' tops within 3 px and every bar within 1 px (T-2524)

Fence: each cap is the shaft's breadth at its top (57 px, 0.51 m, with its eave) and its lower corners flare out like a hood over the heart, a quarter-sine from 1.93 m to 0.56 m across at 1.72 m (63 px), then rounded back in to the shaft by 1.66 m; the model's cap was a plain box; T-2521 read those rows through the camera T-2423 solved, and they are carried here through the one T-2523 re-solved, with the rest of the fence T-2524 re-reads (T-2521, T-2524)

Fence: south of the south pier, read again at 3x (T-2521), the print's 'pale block' is the lawn, in the tone of the lawn between the bars north of the gateway (180-200 against 160-200) under a hedge line at 946 px; a bar stands at 68-70 px hard by the plinth, dark down to the base, and the base runs on under it to the frame, so it is the barred run continuing, as the model builds it; the pale dash at 918 px over those same 20 px stands where the model's own top rail does (925 px), and the 7 px between them falls to the fence's heights T-2524 re-reads

South of the gable: the print's block is the sheet's south projection, not the neighbour (sheet 20 puts 1700 Prairie's north wall 4.4 m south of the front's south end and its front 1.5 m forward of 1638's, so through this camera all of 1700 falls left of the frame), and it is a lower wing: on the sheet's east face (u -6.67 m) its eave's drip reads at 482 px, a wall top 5.03 m over the basement's top (5.98 m over the walk) where the house's flanks stand at 6.03 m; its roof faces the street, a 50-degree gable whose ridge (264 px, horizontal) runs north on the plan's middle into the main roof, its south rake seen edge-on against the sky; and the drip's south corner (88.5 px) puts its verge at v -3.42 m, so its south wall at v -3.0 m, 0.6 m south of the sheet's -2.4 m line (T-2532). On its face two upper lights 0.5 m wide (179-209 and 224-256 px, 522-592 px) and, under them, a light 0.58 m wide and a narrow one 0.22 m wide (190-225 and 154-167 px, 677-737 px), their feet lost in the planting. Rendered: ridge 263 px, drip 480-483 px, the drip's corner 88 px, the four lights within 3 px; the rake's top lands 5-7 px south of the print's (118 against 125 px at 275 px), the print's rake leaning more steeply than a ridge on the plan's middle can draw

South of the gable, at the wing's south corner: a pale upright about 0.6 m wide from under the eave (502 px) to 655 px with a soft south edge, and a third narrow lower light at 110-124 px, at or just past the wall's line; neither is identified (a lit corner, a downpipe or a tree's trunk), and neither is built; the wing's face in the print is dark, in 1700 Prairie's shadow, where the render lights it. Read again (T-2533): both straddle the wing's corner line, which through the camera falls at 117 px (the upright 95-135 px, the light 110-124 px), so neither can stand on the wing's east face, nor on its south face, which an eye 5.7 m north of that wall does not see; and the upright stops under the eave, so it is no chimney. Both are pale where the wall behind is in shade, and the upright's south edge is ragged like the planting's: something in the yard, catching the sun in front of the corner (a trunk or a creeper on a post), not the house. The wing's face is dark because 1700 Prairie, 4.4 m south and outside this record, shades it; the scene, which does not build 1700 here, lights it. So the picture does not show the house at that corner
Left of the wing, the dark mass to the frame's edge and the tree over it: 1700 Prairie's north flank and its yard, outside this record

Planting: the shrubs in front of the bay and along the stoop, and the creeper at the stoop's foot, stand in the yard in front of the basement and the stoop's lowest risers, so the picture does not show how those meet the ground; the planting is the yard's, outside this record
Colour of every surface: the print is a monochrome halftone

Front walk (T-3222): the print shows pale ground through the gateway between the two piers and at the foot of the porch stair behind the fence; the model drew none, the stair coming down on bare ground and the gateway opening on nothing. Now a 1.2 m walk of flags in the plinths' stone comes in through the gateway, runs north along the fence's back and turns west to the stair's foot; through the camera its flags fill the gateway between the plinths and show under the stair's last step where the print's pale ground is. The rest of it is behind the hedge in the print, so its line there is reconstructed
